etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English organe, from Old French organe, from Latin organum, from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon, “an instrument, implement, tool, also an organ of sense or apprehension, an organ of the body, also a musical instrument, an organ”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵ-. Doublet of organon, organum, and orgue.

definitions.definition: The larger part of an organism, composed of tissues that perform similar functions.

quote.citation: 2018, Sandeep Jauhar, Heart: a History, →ISBN, page 98:
quote.text: No matter the extraordinary progress that has been made in heart surgery over the past century, the heart remains a vulnerable organ.

definitions.definition: (by extension) A body of an organization dedicated to the performing of certain functions.

quote.text: This Organ is called a Thermometer, or Thermoscope, because the degrees of Heat and Cold are measured and marked by it.

definitions.definition: (music) A musical instrument that has multiple pipes which play when a key is pressed (the pipe organ), or an electronic instrument designed to replicate such.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter V, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights,  […] , the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.

definitions.definition: An official magazine, newsletter, or similar publication of an organization.

quote.citation: 1920, Edward Carpenter, Pagan and Christian Creeds, New York: Harcourt, Brace and Co., page 81:
quote.text: If the Snake has an unmistakeable resemblance to the male organ in its active state, the foliage of the tree or bush is equally remindful of the female.

definitions.definition: (historical, military) An Asian form of mitrailleuse.

quote.citation: 1790, H. Compton, A particular account of the European military adventurers of Hindustan, from 1784 to 1803, page 61:
quote.text: Lieutenant Roberts was also severely wounded by a missile, or weapon called an Organ, which is composed of about thirty-six gun barrels so joined as to fire at once.

definitions.definition: (obsolete, transitive) To supply with an organ or organs; to fit with organs.

quote.text: Thou art elemented and organ'd for other apprehensions.
